title: Locale-guided translation probe suite (CJK & RTL) - 2026
body:
Purpose:
This is a working probe suite and notes for onboarding models into Redwood's multilingual evaluation flow. Focus areas: CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) layout/width/segmentation, RTL scripts (Arabic/Hebrew) with bidi artifacts, locale-aware formatting (dates, numbers, currency), and translation quality for en<->{CJK,RTL} pairs.

Scope and goals:
- Create a compact but high-coverage prompt set that surfaces common regressions during model updates (kernel/quant changes, tokenization changes, context-length behavior).
- Prioritize failure modes that affect downstream product (generation hallucination on numeric ranges, date formatting inconsistencies, bidi reordering in UI).
- Produce reproducible examples for debug + eval metrics + quick manual spot checks.

Intended consumers:
- Applied ML onboarding engineers
- Model-onboarding SREs running nightly regression jobs
- Product QA when evaluating localization regressions

Quick notes about style for this doc (working):
- Keep prompts short (1-3 sentences) but include explicit locale instructions when testing formatting.
- Include both translation tasks and transformation tasks (e.g., canonicalize phone numbers, normalize dates).
- Mix synthetic and naturally-sourced examples (small sample of real user strings from anonymized logs).

Evaluation matrix (high level):
- Metrics: chrF2, COMET (if available), token-level edit rate, exact-match for canonicalization tasks; locale-formatting F1 for extracted fields.
- Threshold suggestions (initial):
  - chrF2 drop <= 2.5% acceptable for minor changes; >5% requires investigation.
  - COMET delta < -0.1 flagged.
  - Canonicalization exact-match >= 95% for dates and phone numbers.
  - Bidi/visual reordering: manual spot-check on 30 random RTL cases, allow up to 2 fails before escalation.

Prompt buckets and sample probes:
1) Translation short-utterance (literal)
- en -> zh-Hans: "Can you open the door?" -> expect natural zh output with simplified characters and polite modal marker.
- en -> ja: "Where is the nearest train station?" -> expect 地下鉄/駅 phrasing.

2) Translation with numeric contexts
- en -> ko: "The meeting is on 10/11/2026 at 9:00 AM."
  - Check: locale interpretation (is it Oct 11 or Nov 10?)
  - Canonicalization expected: ISO 2026-10-11T09:00:00 or flagged if ambiguous.

3) Date and number formatting (locale instructions explicit)
- Prompt: "Format this date for fr-FR: 2026-03-04" -> expect "04/03/2026".
- Prompt: "Display 1234567.89 in zh-CN currency" -> expect "¥1,234,567.89" or locale-appropriate currency symbol mapping.

4) Phone/currency canonicalization (critical for integrations)
- Examples:
  - "+1 (415) 555-0123" (en-US) -> canonical E.164 "+14155550123"
  - "010-1234-5678" (ko) -> canonical "+821012345678"

5) CJK width and punctuation variants
- Inputs with mixed halfwidth/ fullwidth punctuation and ASCII inside CJK: e.g., "今天是 3/4，天气不错。"
  - Expect consistent normalization rules across models.
- Japanese iteration mark: test "時々" vs repeated kanji sequences to ensure tokenization preserved meaning.

6) RTL bidi pitfalls and mirror-sensitive characters
- Hebrew example: "מתי המשלוח יגיע?" (When will the shipment arrive?)
- Arabic example with parentheses and punctuation: "هل موعدنا (٢٥/١١/٢٠٢٦) ثابت؟"
  - Check: parentheses orientation, numerals left-to-right vs Arabic-Indic digits, and final punctuation placement.
- Include explicit tests with U+200F/U+200E markers to ensure server doesn't strip invisible bidi controls incorrectly.

7) Context preservation with KV cache / partial completions
- Multi-turn short chat where an earlier turn sets locale preferences:
  - Turn 1: "Set preferred locale to ar-EG and date format to DD/MM/YYYY."
  - Turn 2: "Schedule appointment on 03/04/2026."
  - Expect resolved date: 03 April 2026 (not March 4).

8) Translation-quality edgecases (CJK idioms, politeness)
- Japanese honorifics: source contains "〜さん" or "〜様"; check that model preserves appropriate register.
- Chinese idiom compression: literal vs idiomatic translation differences for short sentences.

Test artifact layout (how we store examples):
- filename: probe-[bucket]-[shorttag]-v1.txt (for reproducibility)
- each probe entry: ID | source_locale | target_locale | prompt_text | expected_normalized_output | flags (ambiguous/needs-manual)

Mini sample probe entries (human readable examples):
- P-0001 | en-US | zh-Hans | "Please translate: 'Return by 12/01/2026'" | "请在 2026-12-01 前退回。" | ambiguous-date
- P-0021 | en-GB | ko | "The conference starts on 7/9/2026" | "2026-09-07" | locale-check
- P-0042 | en-US | ar-EG | "Call me at (202) 555-0168" | "+12025550168" | phone-canonicalization

Known flaky areas / hypotheses to validate:
- Tokenizer updates that change token boundaries inside CJK compounds can increase chrF noise even when semantics preserved. We need per-token-diff inspector.
- Quantized kernels sometimes produce swapped punctuation ordering in RTL outputs. Suspect kernel-level character mapping for mirrored glyphs.
- Date normalization brittle when prompt lacks explicit locale; many production prompts are ambiguous. Consider enforcing explicit-locale header in hosted API for eval runs.

Regression run plan (routine):
- Nightly regression job runs on a stable sample (3k probes across locales) with deterministic seeds.
- Run heavier regression on release candidate builds (20k probes) with flagged diffs exported to S3 for manual triage.
- Pager threshold: if canonicalization exact-match drops below 90% on any critical locale -> alert on-call applied-ml and product-l10n.

Debugging checklist when a probe fails:
- Re-run with deterministic seed and log tokenization boundaries.
- Compare tokenizer outputs between model versions.
- Check for presence/absence of bidi control chars in raw output.
- Confirm whether fallback model routing changed (e.g., quantized variant returned instead of fp16).
- Attach minimal repro snippet and open MLINF ticket with examples.

Notes about human evaluation and spot checks:
- For bidi and visual ordering, automated metrics are insufficient; schedule weekly human spot-checks for 50 high-risk probes.
- For idiom/politeness, have bilingual annotators provide 3-way labels: correct, acceptable, incorrect.

Operational suggestions for platform integration:
- Add a header in inference calls: X-Expected-Locale: {locale} and X-Format-Profile: {profile-id} so offline eval can simulate exact production behavior.
- Bundle a minimal normalization library used in canonicalization tasks to reduce evaluator variance (ex: shared E.164 phone normalizer, CLDR-based date formatters).

Open TODOs (short):
- [ ] Expand RTL numeric coverage to include Arabic-Indic digits and Western digits mixed cases (owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Add 400+ synthetic CJK compound tokens to stress tokenizers (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Finalize exact metric thresholds with product (owner: Elena).
- [ ] Wire alpha-version of header-driven eval into regression runner (owner: Connor).

References / links for locale rules:
- CLDR rules quick reference: https://cldr.org/
- Internal tokenization diff tool: https://internal.redwood/tools/token-diff

Appendix: quick prompt examples to copy-paste into sandbox
- "Translate to zh-Hant: 'The shipment was dispatched on 2026-11-25.'"
- "Normalize this phone number for JP: 03-1234-5678"
- "You are a translator. Output date in format YYYY-MM-DD for locale ja-JP: '10/11/2026'"
- Arabic bidi test: "Translate to ar: 'Our meeting (12/05/2026) is confirmed.'"

Notes-to-self (fragments):
- keep prompt templates under 200 chars where possible.
- align with product's canonicalization microservice outputs to reduce false positives.
- consider light-weight visual diff tool for RTL string rendering (screenshot-based) if we still see noisy failures.

Last updated by Maya — will iterate after first nightly run with new tokenizer build.
